Bridge’s bid box as a chooser

Today the box asks “What’s your bid?” A tap on a suit sends your bid at once. Here the levels and the suits are choosers like the suit pill. You pick a level and a suit. The yellow button shows your bid. A tap on it sends it. Pass, Double and Redouble stay under it. Tap the cells to try each version. A switch changes every version at once. Every piece is drawn by the site’s own stylesheet.

What changes for the player

Today a bid is two taps. It goes the moment you tap the suit. With a chooser it is three taps, for the level, the suit and then the button. The extra tap lets you read your bid on the button before it goes. That matters on a phone, where a slip of the thumb sends the wrong suit today. A bid cannot be taken back. Pass, Double and Redouble stay one tap.

The title goes. The notice at the top of the table asks “What’s your bid?” instead, as it already does on a phone on its side when the box has no room for its title.

The suits keep Bridge’s ranking, clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades and no trump, and not the site’s own order (clubs, diamonds, spades and hearts), which every other suit chooser uses. Bids rank that way, so after a bid every bid you can make stays to its right (your choice, 2 Oct 2026).

On a phone held upright the seven levels take a row of narrower cells (28px rather than 32), since the room between the side players’ cards is 202px. Today’s box solves the same room with two rows of levels.

Questions for you

  • Today or a chooser? If a chooser, is it version 1, 2 or 3?
  • What should the button say? “Bid 3♥” with your bid in it, “Bid”, or “Choose”?
  • Should the chooser start empty or with the lowest bid picked? The suit pill starts with its first suit picked. With the lowest bid picked, one tap on the button makes that bid.
  • How wide? As wide as today’s box so every row lines up? Or with square cells like the suit pill, so the chooser is narrower than the buttons under it?
  • Which mark for the picked cell? Today’s mark or the white card from the suit chooser lab (suit-chooser-lab.html)?

How it would be built

It is for the redesign only. The old look keeps today’s box. Table.showTrumpPill draws one row of suits. A bid chooser needs two rows with a pick each. Its cells must also carry a number or “NT”. In bridge-game-ui.js, showBidPanel would draw the chooser instead of the twelve buttons, keep the picked level and suit, and send them from the button (clicks.handleBidClick(level, strain)). In bridge-layout.js the box, its head and the twelve button spots give way to the chooser, the button and the calls. pieces.scss gains a text cell and a mark per row, the two proposal rules at the bottom of chooser-lab-parts/lab.css.
